decisions.reason: Because it is close to the core decorative assortment and the firm has enough warehouse and service slack to carry uncertain collection items, management would likely keep it unless sales clearly miss aspiration levels.

Because this transparent burnout fabric fits the established decorative business but is design-sensitive and somewhat uncertain, management would keep it while monitoring whether it reaches the performance expected for comparable collection products.

Because it overlaps with the other burnout launches and there is no visible sign of standout traction, management would be somewhat more likely to drop it and reallocate shelf space and attention if it underperforms aspiration.

Because velour-like upholstery fabric builds directly on the established offer and uses existing sampling, sewing, and stocked-distribution capabilities, management would tend to keep it while demand becomes clearer.
Because the flame-retardant functional niche broadens the range in a way that fits the firm's dependable-supply strengths, management would usually retain it unless results are clearly below target.
Because lining fabric is a practical complement to the core textile assortment and can be supported with existing logistics at low additional cost, management would more likely keep it than drop it.
